Summary: Reusable software-development child process that breaks implementation into intake, architecture, optional solution setup, feature/function implementation, unit tests, and evidence handoff.
ValueStatement: Keeps a large implementation lane observable and manager-reportable by using small process steps plus nested setup and feature/function implementation subprocesses.
InterfaceContractSummary: The parent process supplies the change scope, repository target, architecture decision, and validation bar; this subprocess returns implementation and test evidence.
GovernanceNotes: Implementation work must remain split into typed, observable steps so blockers can be reported by managers without reading raw execution threads.
ChangeSummary: Adds the default atomic implementation subprocess used by the software-delivery process.
GovernancePolicySummary: A development slice cannot close until code change, tests, and validation evidence are durable and linked to the parent scope.
ConstitutionRuleSummary: The parent and child runs share process identity through explicit runtime relationships, not duplicated state or chat summaries.
OperatingModeSummary: Assisted execution with manager observation; process-level manager override can replace default HR matching for manager roles.
SimulationReadinessSummary: Small enough for real local validation while still exercising nested subprocess creation and child-run observation.
Metrics: Number of implementation slices completed without parent-step blockage.
Time spent blocked in scaffold, implementation, and validation phases.
Share of slices with test evidence attached before parent peer review.
Risks: Nested setup subprocess is used for an existing solution without explicit tailoring.
Code implementation expands beyond the approved slice boundary.
Validation evidence is missing or too broad to explain failures.
TailoringRules: Skip the generic .NET solution setup subprocess only when the repository already has a correct solution skeleton and the skip records explicit proof.
Use the app archetype, test framework, validation type, and product root from the current project structure or upstream architecture notes; escalate when those inputs conflict or are missing.

When the parent scope is a simple full app or one-shot full deliverable, keep every explicitly named core MVP behavior in this development slice and pass those criteria into the feature/function child subprocess. The MVP must not be scaffold-only, setup-only, naming-only, readiness-only, static-looking, or build-only proof; scaffolding is prerequisite evidence, not the accepted product behavior.

Split work into multiple instances only when the parent launch context supplies an explicit remaining-slice schedule. Without that schedule, do not defer a named core interaction, persistence requirement, calculation, search, dashboard, or recovery behavior to an unplanned later slice.
Keep parent approval and release gates in the parent process; this subprocess owns implementation proof only.

RoleUsages.Purpose: Report progress, blockers, and child subprocess status to the parent process.
RoleUsages.StaffingIntent: A manager-capable human or AI agent that can summarize high-volume execution data.

RoleUsages.Purpose: Confirm the slice fits the parent architecture and does not create hidden source-of-truth drift.
RoleUsages.StaffingIntent: Architecture reviewer for scoped design decisions and integration risks.

RoleUsages.Purpose: Implement the bounded change and maintain tests.
Confirm the implementation has focused tests and regression evidence.
RoleUsages.StaffingIntent: A reviewer capable of interpreting targeted test, build, and browser proof.

Steps.Title: Capture implementation slice boundary
Steps.Subtitle: Small enough to finish
Steps.Notes: Restate the parent scope as one bounded implementation slice with assumptions, exclusions, and validation hooks. If the parent asks for a simple full app or one-shot broad deliverable, retain every explicitly named core MVP behavior from upstream project-structure and architecture facts. The MVP must not be scaffold-only, setup-only, naming-only, readiness-only, static-looking, or build-only; it must include the complete recognizable interaction path, typed state transitions, and any named persistence, calculation, search, dashboard, or recovery behavior. Exclude only optional polish or a capability assigned to an explicit later-slice schedule. If project structure lists visual target assets, copy their ImageAsset node ids, media paths, and target-look notes into the slice acceptance criteria or validation hooks. This is an intake step: do not run restore, build, test, app startup, or browser validation here.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Parent scope packet, repository context, and requested behavior.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Slice boundary with acceptance criteria, product-root intent, setup needs, and excluded follow-up work.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Scope summary, assumptions, product-root classification, setup/implementation handoff, and validation plan outline.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Slice manager can narrow execution scope but cannot silently discard parent acceptance criteria or downgrade a requested product to scaffold-only readiness.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Block when the slice cannot be made small enough for atomic validation, when the selected scope is only scaffold/setup/readiness work, or when the required product root, architecture, app archetype, or validation boundary is contradictory or missing.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Rebind only to a manager-capable operator that can report to the parent run.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Implementation slice scope packet
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable by parent peer review and future slices.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must define acceptance criteria, exclusions, intended product root, setup needs, and validation hooks without using build/runtime/browser proof as intake evidence.

Steps.Title: Check architecture and source-of-truth impact
Steps.Subtitle: No hidden ownership drift
Steps.Notes: Confirm canonical models, integration boundaries, persistence ownership, and UI/application/domain responsibilities before code starts. This architecture step must not run restore, build, test, app startup, browser proof, or product-root file inspection for a missing greenfield root; record the intended root and setup handoff instead.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Slice scope packet and parent architecture notes.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Architecture decision record or explicit no-ADR rationale for this slice.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Touched boundaries, source-of-truth decision, and risk notes.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Slice architect can require split or escalation when ownership boundaries are unclear.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Block on canonical model ambiguity, persistence ownership conflict, unsafe cross-layer leakage, contradictory project-structure requirements, or artifact recovery when required architecture evidence is missing or invalid before branch routing. Do not block only because a greenfield product root does not exist yet.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Rebind only to an architect-capable reviewer.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Slice architecture decision record
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable by implementation, peer review, and parent release approval.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must name source-of-truth ownership and cross-layer impact.

Steps.Title: Prepare solution skeleton subprocess
Steps.Subtitle: Nested scaffold run
Steps.Notes: Launch the generic .NET solution setup subprocess when the slice starts from an empty or incomplete .NET solution. The child process must choose the app archetype and test framework from project structure or architecture notes, not from process-specific assumptions. Accept either setup-handoff or setup-handoff-after-repair from the child as valid setup proof; treat setup-repair-escalation as no-go blocker evidence.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Slice scope, architecture decision, and target solution naming contract.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Observed child run that creates or validates the solution skeleton and test project.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Child run status, build proof, setup-handoff or setup-handoff-after-repair packet, and setup-repair-escalation no-go evidence when present.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Implementation engineer may skip only when an equivalent solution skeleton already exists and evidence is recorded.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Block the slice when the child setup run blocks, fails, reports setup-repair-escalation, or lacks setup-handoff/setup-handoff-after-repair scaffold proof.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Rebind only to a .NET-capable implementer that can coordinate setup evidence and child run output.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Solution skeleton evidence
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable by implementation and validation steps.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must point to the observed child run, setup-handoff or setup-handoff-after-repair scaffold proof, or an explicit already-existing skeleton proof. setup-repair-escalation is blocker evidence, not accepted setup proof.

Steps.Title: Implement bounded code change through subprocess
Steps.Subtitle: Observed feature run
Steps.Notes: Launch the feature/function implementation subprocess for the bounded behavior in this slice. First call project_structure_process_subprocess_launch with definitionKey dotnet-feature-function-implementation; do not wait silently or return Blocked before attempting that child launch unless mandatory launch inputs are missing. Before launch, carry forward the concrete MVP behavior, product root, app archetype, setup handoff, acceptance criteria, validation hooks, and exclusions from the slice artifacts so the child receives one implementable request. When the slice scope includes visual target ImageAsset ids or media paths, include them in the child request and require the visible implementation to use those assets as the design target. Do not launch this child when the slice scope only asks for scaffold readiness, solution setup, naming, or generic app-shell existence. If the launch response includes ParentDeferredOutcomeJson, submit that parent outcome exactly: active child runs defer the parent, completed child runs complete the parent from child evidence, and stopped child runs propagate their concrete blocker. Observe the child run status, change-set artifact, validation evidence, accepted handoff artifacts, repair escalation artifacts, blockers, and manager-directed rework without duplicating child runtime state in this parent step.

AcceptedChildOutputs.ArtifactTitle: Feature implementation handoff packet after repair
Feature repair escalation packet for parent review
Feature repair recheck escalation evidence for parent review

Steps.InputContractSummary: Slice scope, architecture decision, solution skeleton evidence, and one bounded feature or function request derived from the parent scope when needed.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Observed child run that returns a reviewable code change, focused validation evidence, blockers, and residual risks.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Child run status, implementation change set, validation evidence, accepted handoff evidence, repair escalation evidence, manager rework directives, and unresolved blockers.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Implementation engineer can request targeted child-run repair but cannot widen behavior beyond the slice boundary.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Block the slice when the child implementation run blocks or fails without a typed output. Materialize a completed feature-repair-escalation packet as review evidence so add-tests-and-proof can select slice-repair-required; do not treat that packet as accepted implementation proof.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Rebind only to a .NET-capable implementer that can observe child implementation runs and request targeted rework.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Slice implementation change set
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable by tests, peer review, and parent QA.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must point to the observed child implementation run and include changed files, behavioral intent, touched-surface inventory, validation proof summary, and accepted handoff evidence from feature-handoff or feature-handoff-after-repair. A feature-repair-escalation packet is blocker evidence, not accepted implementation proof.

Steps.Title: Validate tests and targeted proof
Steps.Subtitle: Validation commands before handoff
Steps.Notes: Review the current-run implement-code-change coordinator artifact, test additions, and validation evidence, then run targeted build and test validation needed to prove the slice behavior. This step has validation-command ownership: do not defer restore, build, or test execution to later root proof steps. Use the governed validation tools workspace_dotnet_restore, workspace_dotnet_build, and workspace_dotnet_test for the current run. If current-run restore/build/test receipts are missing and those validation tools plus the grounded product root are available, run the validation chain now; missing receipts are not a repair finding by themselves. Managed artifact evidence rule: cite this step's managed artifact and current-run validation tool receipts as proof. Do not put product source/test file aliases, native product paths, external-target file paths, managed-files paths, or project-media storage paths in evidenceRefs. In the artifact body, prefer product-root-relative file names. If a retry diagnostic names an ungrounded product path but the grounded product root and validation tools are available, rerun the restore/build/test chain or read/list the file with a current-run workspace tool, then overwrite the artifact with grounded receipt-based proof instead of selecting slice-repair-required or returning Blocked. For .NET product roots, run and record a current-run validation chain: dotnet restore, dotnet build --no-restore, and dotnet test --no-restore when a test project exists or tests are expected. Target restore/build at the discovered solution when present; target workspace_dotnet_test at DotNetTestProjectFileAlias or DotNetTestProjectFile when present, preferably with noBuild=true after a successful solution build, and use the solution target for tests only when no test project target exists. Do not mark the slice accepted from implementation handoff evidence alone, and do not select slice-repair-required only because the receipts were absent before this step ran. External generated product roots may not be Git repositories. Do not call workspace_git_status as a validation precondition for a grounded product root, and do not treat a not a git repository result as a product-root, validation-tool, or repair blocker. If Git status was already attempted and failed only because the product root is not a Git repository, record Git status as not applicable and continue immediately with product-root file listing plus the restore/build/test validation chain. Before running validation commands, resolve the actual solution target from setup handoff, product readback, or product-root file listing: inspect <ProductRoot>/<SolutionName>.slnx and <ProductRoot>/<SolutionName>.sln, use the existing file, prefer .slnx when both exist, and never synthesize or require <SolutionName>.sln when only <SolutionName>.slnx exists. If a validation attempt fails only because a guessed solution path is missing, rerun the current-run validation chain against the discovered .slnx or .sln target and do not route repair for the missing guessed path. If --no-restore fails because restore assets are stale or missing, run restore and then rerun build/test; select slice-repair-required only when the restored validation chain still fails or product proof does not satisfy the chosen slice behavior. Child-run refs cited inside the coordinator artifact are trace links, not direct read requirements for this QA validation step; do not read artifacts/process-runs/<child-run-id>/... files directly unless the step brief explicitly lists that exact child artifact as a required upstream ref. If the coordinator artifact says the child completed and lists accepted handoff evidence, independently validate from the product root with build/test/readback proof instead of returning Blocked for the child artifact boundary. Do not launch the app, open a browser, or capture runtime screenshots in this slice proof step; root runtime-command and screenshot writeback steps own live visual proof. Do not add, edit, or repair product tests in this step; missing or inadequate tests must select the slice-repair-required branch and route back to a bounded implementation repair subprocess instead of being silently fixed by QA. When visual target ImageAsset ids or media paths are part of the slice scope, verify that coordinator evidence preserves those acceptance inputs and require root runtime-command and screenshot writeback follow-up for live screenshot comparison before release. When selecting slice-repair-required, write a repair target packet in this step artifact with exact failed acceptance criteria, failing command or evidence metric, child run id when present, child step artifact refs as trace links when present, and the smallest proof that would close the defect. If the current-run coordinator packet cites a child feature-repair-escalation or targeted-recheck artifact but direct child reads are not allowed, restate the missing or failing evidence from the coordinator packet and product proof instead of returning Blocked. Return blocked only for environment, permission, unavailable validation tool, or process-contract failures that prevent validation or repair routing.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Authoritative slice scope packet, implementation change set, and slice architecture decision; every named core criterion remains in scope until directly proved.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Test and validation evidence review tied to the implemented behavior, with explicit slice-accepted or slice-repair-required branch.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Current-run restore/build/test commands, exit codes, warnings, executed tests, explicit assessment of whether current-run coordinator evidence and product proof satisfy acceptance criteria, and a concrete repair target packet whenever repair is selected. Live runtime screenshots are owned by root runtime-command and screenshot writeback steps.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Validation owner can accept evidence or require focused implementation rework when proof or tests do not match acceptance criteria, but cannot mutate product files.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Select slice-repair-required on missing tests, failing build, failing focused validation, validation too broad to diagnose failures, missing accepted child proof in the current-run coordinator artifact, or invalid evidence that still has a repair route. Block only when the environment, permissions, validation tooling, or process contract prevents validation or repair routing.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Rebind only to a reviewer capable of evaluating targeted test evidence.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Slice test evidence
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable by parent QA and release approval.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must include current-run restore/build/test commands, exit codes, executed-test counts when a test project exists or tests are expected, proof tied to acceptance criteria, and review of current-run coordinator evidence plus product readback. If tests, accepted child handoff in the coordinator artifact, or other acceptance evidence are missing or inadequate, the artifact must route repair to implementation with an exact repair target packet instead of recording QA-authored product changes or generic residual risk. Live browser proof belongs to root runtime-command and screenshot writeback steps.

BranchOutcomes.Title: Slice accepted
BranchOutcomes.Description: Slice validation evidence is sufficient for parent handoff.

BranchOutcomes.Title: Slice repair required
BranchOutcomes.Description: Slice validation found missing tests, failed proof, missing accepted child handoff, or another concrete issue requiring bounded implementation repair.

RequiredReceipts.Reason: Slice validation must run restore in the current execution before choosing accepted or repair-required.
Slice validation must run build in the current execution before choosing accepted or repair-required.
Slice validation must run tests in the current execution when a test project exists or tests are expected.

Steps.Title: Hand off implementation slice
Steps.Subtitle: Parent-ready accepted evidence
Steps.Notes: Summarize the initially accepted slice path, produced evidence, residual risks, and recommended parent-process next action.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Scope, architecture, accepted change set, and accepted test evidence.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Parent-ready implementation handoff with blockers and residual risks.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Implementation summary, validation result, open issues, and explicit next action.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Slice manager can close only when slice-accepted was selected and validation evidence is present.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Do not close on the initial path when validation selected repair-required, tests fail, blockers remain untriaged, or the parent cannot determine next action.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Rebind only to a manager-capable operator that can report to the parent run.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Implementation slice handoff packet
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable by parent peer review, QA, and release approval.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must summarize change, test evidence, unresolved risks, and recommended next action.

Steps.Title: Repair slice findings through subprocess
Steps.Subtitle: Bounded repair child run
Steps.Notes: Launch a feature/function implementation subprocess for the concrete slice validation findings. First call project_structure_process_subprocess_launch with definitionKey dotnet-feature-function-implementation; do not wait silently or return Blocked before attempting that child launch unless mandatory repair-launch inputs are missing. Carry forward the exact repair target packet from add-tests-and-proof, including failed acceptance criteria, failing command or browser metrics, child run id, child step artifact refs, product root, app archetype, setup handoff, accepted slice boundary, exclusions, and the smallest proof that would close the defect. Do not ask the child subprocess to select a fresh MVP behavior; this is a repair launch and the child feature scope must inherit the repair target as mandatory acceptance criteria. If the launch response includes ParentDeferredOutcomeJson, submit that parent outcome exactly: active child runs defer the parent, completed child runs complete the parent from child evidence, and stopped child runs propagate their concrete blocker. The child repair run must return accepted handoff evidence or explicit repair escalation evidence.

AcceptedChildOutputs.ArtifactTitle: Feature implementation handoff packet after repair

Steps.InputContractSummary: Authoritative slice scope packet plus the exact validation failure, repair target packet, implementation change set, architecture decision, and bounded repair request; the latest defect must not narrow away other core criteria.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Observed child repair run with change set, validation proof, accepted handoff, or reviewable repair escalation evidence for the parent recheck.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Child repair run status, changed files, validation evidence, accepted handoff evidence, repair escalation evidence, and unresolved blockers.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Implementation engineer can request bounded repair but cannot widen the slice beyond the parent-approved boundary.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Block when the child repair run itself blocks or fails. Materialize a completed child repair-escalation packet for parent recheck and manager-assisted recovery; do not treat that packet as accepted product proof.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Rebind only to a .NET-capable implementer that can observe child repair runs and request targeted rework.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Slice repair change set
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable by repaired slice recheck, parent QA, and release approval.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must point to the observed child repair implementation run and include changed files, behavioral intent, proof summary mapped to the original repair target, and accepted handoff evidence from feature-handoff or feature-handoff-after-repair. A feature-repair-escalation packet is blocker evidence, not accepted repair proof.

Steps.Title: Recheck slice proof after repair
Steps.Subtitle: Repaired validation commands
Steps.Notes: Review the current-run repair coordinator artifacts and rerun the smallest reliable proof needed for the slice. This step has validation-command ownership after repair: do not defer restore, build, or test execution to later root proof steps. Use the governed validation tools workspace_dotnet_restore, workspace_dotnet_build, and workspace_dotnet_test for the current run. If current-run restore/build/test receipts are missing and those validation tools plus the grounded product root are available, run the validation chain now; missing receipts are not an escalation finding by themselves. Managed artifact evidence rule: cite this step's managed artifact and current-run validation tool receipts as proof. Do not put product source/test file aliases, native product paths, external-target file paths, managed-files paths, or project-media storage paths in evidenceRefs. In the artifact body, prefer product-root-relative file names. If a retry diagnostic names an ungrounded product path but the grounded product root and validation tools are available, rerun the restore/build/test chain or read/list the file with a current-run workspace tool, then overwrite the artifact with grounded receipt-based proof instead of selecting slice-repair-escalation or returning Blocked. For .NET product roots, run and record a current-run validation chain: dotnet restore, dotnet build --no-restore, and dotnet test --no-restore when a test project exists or tests are expected. Target restore/build at the discovered solution when present; target workspace_dotnet_test at DotNetTestProjectFileAlias or DotNetTestProjectFile when present, preferably with noBuild=true after a successful solution build, and use the solution target for tests only when no test project target exists. Do not accept the repair from child handoff text alone, and do not select slice-repair-escalation only because the receipts were absent before this step ran. External generated product roots may not be Git repositories. Do not call workspace_git_status as a validation precondition for a grounded product root, and do not treat a not a git repository result as a product-root, validation-tool, or repair blocker. If Git status was already attempted and failed only because the product root is not a Git repository, record Git status as not applicable and continue immediately with product-root file listing plus the restore/build/test validation chain. Before running validation commands, resolve the actual solution target from setup handoff, repaired evidence, product readback, or product-root file listing: inspect <ProductRoot>/<SolutionName>.slnx and <ProductRoot>/<SolutionName>.sln, use the existing file, prefer .slnx when both exist, and never synthesize or require <SolutionName>.sln when only <SolutionName>.slnx exists. If prior validation failed only because a guessed solution path was missing, rerun the current-run validation chain against the discovered .slnx or .sln target before selecting slice-repair-escalation. If --no-restore fails because restore assets are stale or missing, run restore and then rerun build/test; select slice-repair-escalation only when the restored validation chain still fails or product proof does not satisfy the original repair target. Child-run refs cited inside add-tests-and-proof or slice-repair-code-change are trace links, not direct read requirements for this QA validation step; do not read artifacts/process-runs/<child-run-id>/... files directly unless the step brief explicitly lists that exact child artifact as a required upstream ref. Select slice-accepted only when repaired evidence, current-run build proof, current-run executed-test proof when tests exist or are expected, and focused proof satisfy the slice behavior and the original repair target. Select slice-repair-escalation when the original repair target proof still fails, accepted child handoff is missing from the current-run repair coordinator artifact, the child proved a different behavior while leaving the triggering failure unresolved, or another repair would exceed the slice boundary.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Authoritative slice scope packet, original validation failure, repair child evidence, and architecture decision; recheck must account for every original core criterion.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Repaired slice validation evidence with explicit slice-accepted or slice-repair-escalation branch.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Current-run restore/build/test commands, exit codes, warnings, executed tests, current-run repair coordinator evidence, original repair target before/after assessment, and unresolved gaps after repair. Live runtime/browser proof belongs to root runtime-command and screenshot writeback steps.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Validation owner can accept repaired evidence or escalate unresolved repair findings; QA still cannot mutate product files.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Select slice-repair-escalation when proof remains failing, missing, detached, or unmapped after repair. Block only when an environment, permission, or process-contract issue prevents recheck execution.

Manager reviews unresolved repaired findings before parent escalation.

Steps.Title: Prepare manager-assisted slice repair
Steps.Subtitle: Manager diagnosis handoff
Steps.Notes: Record unresolved repaired validation findings as a manager diagnosis input. The absence of an accepted child handoff is a routing symptom, not itself a repair target, and the downstream quality-repair subprocess cannot manufacture a child handoff. Preserve the authoritative slice scope, trace why the child withheld acceptance back to the unresolved product behavior or executable proof, distinguish repeated implementation strategy from the acceptance contract, and identify the owning source, failed proof, and smallest mutation-plus-validation loop. Green restore/build/test receipts do not make a presentational shell or missing original workflow proof-only. This artifact is reviewable recovery evidence, not a parent no-go or accepted product proof.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Authoritative slice scope, original validation failure, repair child run evidence, and failed repaired recheck evidence.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Manager repair diagnosis packet with unresolved defects, proof gaps, repeated-strategy analysis, and a bounded mutation-plus-validation target.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Unresolved blocker list, failing proof references, attempted repair, authoritative acceptance criteria, owning source, and recommended manager-assisted repair action.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Slice manager can sequence one diagnosis-guided quality repair subprocess but cannot present unresolved findings as accepted.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Do not continue to parent-ready accepted handoff while repaired validation remains unresolved; prepare the bounded manager-assisted repair unless a genuine permission, environment, or contradictory-requirement blocker prevents it.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Rebind only to a manager-capable operator that can report no-go evidence to the parent run.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Slice repair escalation packet
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable by parent peer review, incident review, and future repair planning.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must summarize unresolved findings, attempted repair, failing proof, no-go rationale, and required next scope.

Steps.Title: Run manager-assisted quality repair
Steps.Subtitle: Diagnosis, implementation, independent validation, and bounded bughunt
Steps.Notes: Launch and observe the dotnet-quality-repair subprocess for the unresolved slice findings. First call project_structure_process_subprocess_launch with definitionKey dotnet-quality-repair. Do not wait silently, write a progress artifact, or create another child while one is active. If the launch response includes ParentDeferredOutcomeJson, submit that parent outcome exactly so the runtime resumes this step from the child result. The child receives the authoritative slice scope, both validation packets, the failed repair evidence, and the manager diagnosis. It owns diagnosis, product mutation, independent validation, and one specialist-guided re-repair before an explicit no-go. This parent step only coordinates the child and materializes accepted handoff evidence; it must not mutate the product or reinterpret a quality-repair-no-go packet as success.
Steps.SubprocessDefinitionSnapshotName: .NET quality repair with diagnosis and bounded bughunt
Steps.InputContractSummary: Authoritative slice scope, original and repaired validation failures, failed child repair evidence, and manager diagnosis; repair action may narrow but acceptance scope may not.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Accepted manager-assisted repair change set with independent validation and optional bughunt evidence, or explicit bounded child no-go.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Child status, diagnosis, product mutation, restore/build/test proof, owning-source readback, optional runtime/browser proof, bughunt evidence when used, and accepted or no-go handoff.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Delivery manager owns repair sequencing; implementation and independent validation remain separate child roles.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Block only when the child blocks, fails, or returns quality-repair-no-go after its bounded diagnosis and bughunt lanes. Do not relaunch the same failed feature-repair strategy.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Manager-assisted repair observation remains with a manager-capable role.
Engineering reviews the bounded repair scope without replacing independent child validation.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Manager-assisted slice repair change set
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable by parent QA, release approval, and later defect analysis.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must point to an accepted dotnet-quality-repair child handoff with diagnosis, changed files, current-execution validation, and confirmation that the original slice criteria remain covered.

Steps.Title: Hand off manager-repaired implementation slice
Steps.Subtitle: Parent-ready manager-assisted evidence
Steps.Notes: Produce the parent-ready handoff only after the manager-assisted quality repair subprocess returned accepted handoff evidence. Reconcile that evidence with every criterion in the authoritative slice scope and state the owning production surface and proof for each core behavior. Do not present a quality-repair-no-go or unresolved criterion as accepted.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Authoritative slice scope, manager diagnosis, and accepted manager-assisted repair change set with independent validation.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Parent-ready implementation handoff after manager-assisted repair with criterion coverage and residual risks.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Manager diagnosis, changed product surfaces, independent validation, bughunt evidence when used, criterion coverage, open risks, and explicit parent next action.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Delivery manager can close only from accepted manager-assisted repair evidence and full criterion coverage.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Do not close when accepted child handoff is missing, any authoritative core criterion remains unresolved, or the child returned no-go.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Rebind only to a manager-capable operator that can reconcile accepted repair evidence with the parent scope.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Implementation slice handoff after manager-assisted repair
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable by parent peer review, QA, and release approval.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must include accepted manager-assisted repair evidence, independent validation, criterion-by-criterion scope coverage, unresolved risks, and recommended parent action.
